correctness.rationale: Prime-power factors p^a, a>=2 make p divide psi(n), violating residue one; an even squarefree composite also contradicts parity. For any remaining odd squarefree composite n, (psi(n)-1)/n is an odd integer >=3, hence psi(n)/n>3. The pairwise obstruction q=-1 mod r forces support primes into one of fifteen explicitly compatible intersections S of B={3,5,7,11,13}. The t smallest eligible primes dominate the Euler factors of any t-element support. Exact integer products of the first 709 eligible primes for all fifteen S are <3; independently reproduced the prime sieve and rational comparisons, including maximum S={11,13}, ratio approximately 2.99970965505, q_709=6661 and the 710th q=6673. This establishes all n without size cutoff; a scan through n<=100000 is not the unbounded proof.

value.rationale: A 710-prime-support necessary condition addresses an explicit natural open congruence primality criterion, not an arbitrary finite cutoff. The fifteen-branch rational certificate plus an unbounded domination argument yields information no finite n-range search could establish.

final_claim: For every integer n>1 with at most 709 distinct prime factors, Dedekind psi satisfies psi(n)=1 modulo n if and only if n is prime. A hypothetical composite has to be odd squarefree with >=710 distinct prime factors.
limitations: No claim that the residue-one conjecture holds for arbitrary n or that any composite counterexample exists.
